case_title: Bhadresh Bipinbhai Sheth v. State of Gujarat & Another
accused_victim_relationship: Neighbour (acquaintance; the judgment says they were known to each other)
evidence_type: Complainant's statements (complaint dated 29.05.2001 and statement dated 31.05.2001); statements of NGO counsellors; no medical or recovery evidence noted
aggravating_circumstances: Alleged only by the prosecutrix: repeated rape after threats, threats to defame via letters, threat involving photographs, alleged interest in her daughter. The Court made no finding on these.
mitigating_circumstances: Accused participated in proceedings since 2001; no allegation of flight or witness influence; investigation complete
trial_court_outcome: No trial verdict. Additional Sessions Judge granted anticipatory bail on 18.05.2013 on conditions; trial on the s.376 charge not concluded
high_court_outcome: Revision allowed on 18.07.2014; anticipatory bail cancelled
neutral_facts: The victim alleged that the accused, a neighbour known to her, asked her to sit in his car at a bus stand around 1997-98. She initially refused but got in. The accused then drove to an uninhabited place, beat her and had sexual intercourse with her against her wishes, threatening her not to disclose the incident. The victim alleged that about a month later the accused repeated the act at a hotel and told her he had taken her photographs. After she moved to another area, the accused allegedly sent letters threatening to defame her. The victim told her husband and in-laws and lodged a complaint with an NGO, followed by a complaint to the Assistant Police Commissioner, Crime Branch, dated 29 May 2001. Two days later, a statement recorded by the investigating officer contained allegations of harassment, blackmail and abusive behaviour but did not mention rape. Counsellors at the NGO stated that the victim had told them about the alleged rape. The victim also alleged threats to her family and that the accused had shown interest in her daughter. The investigation was completed and a revised chargesheet stated that a prima facie case under s.376 IPC was also made out.
attempt_completion: Completed (as alleged by the victim; not adjudicated)
physical_harm: Alleged beating and rape of the victim; no medical findings stated
number_of_offences: 2 charged (IPC s.506(2) and s.376); 0 finally upheld (no conviction; anticipatory bail matter)
key_evidence_accepted: None accepted on merits. The Court expressly declined to assess the evidence and left the findings on the rape charge to the trial court
witness_credibility: Not assessed. The Court left the delay in the complaint and the credibility of the allegations to trial
post_offence_conduct: Accused participated in the proceedings; no allegation he tried to influence witnesses during this period (per Court). The Court noted the prosecutrix's allegation of new breach of bail conditions but did not examine it
custody_duration: Not stated (custody order was stayed; no period of custody given)
bail_history: Bail granted in the 2001 case; custody order of 25.04.2013 stayed; anticipatory bail granted 18.05.2013 by Sessions Court; cancelled by High Court 18.07.2014; restored by Supreme Court
trial_duration: offence: 1997-98 (as alleged); trial judgment: not given; High Court: 18.07.2014; Supreme Court: 01.09.2015
legal_representation: Accused: Dushyant Dave, Harin Raval and others. State: Ms. Hemantika Wahi (prosecutrix appeared in person)
investigation_status: FIR registered 31.05.2001 under IPC s.506(2); further investigation under s.173(8) CrPC; revised chargesheet adding s.376 IPC; investigation complete
procedural_irregularity: The FIR was based on a statement that omitted rape allegations made earlier to NGO and ACP; the Court noted the omission but left it for trial. Charge was framed only under s.506(2) in 2001; s.376 added only in 2014 after delay
appeal_history: Trial court/Sessions: anticipatory bail granted 18.05.2013. High Court: revision allowed, bail cancelled 18.07.2014. Supreme Court: appeals allowed, High Court order set aside, bail restored
prosecution_argument: State (Ms. Hemantika Wahi) argued that once the serious non-bailable s.376 charge was added, the accused should surrender and seek regular bail. Prosecutrix argued the sexual intercourse was rape and that the accused harassed and blackmailed her
defence_argument: Accused argued the relationship was consensual; no rape allegation in the 31.05.2001 statement; long delay of over 9 years before the s.376 application; NGO noting to keep the matter pending; the High Court's findings were not based on record
legal_principle_applied: Anticipatory bail under s.438 CrPC; seriousness of the charge alone is not a bar; balance of the factors in Sibbia and Siddharam (flight risk, witness tampering, role, delay, investigation status)
precedent_relied_upon: Gurbaksh Singh Sibbia and Others v. State of Punjab (1980) 2 SCC 565 (followed); Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra (2011) 1 SCC 694 (referred to)
judicial_mitigating_factors: Delay of about 9 years by the prosecutrix before the s.376 application; the alleged offence is about 17 years old; the investigation is complete; no risk of flight or witness influence; accused participated in all proceedings
judicial_aggravating_factors: None. The Court acknowledged the seriousness of the s.376 charge but held it was not by itself a ground to deny bail
other_sentence_order: Direction for expeditious trial within one year; prosecutrix at liberty to apply to the trial court for cancellation of bail; Supreme Court expressed no view on the merits of that application
